companyDescription: Autonomous sidewalk delivery robots · fleet across 44 cities — but Uber, the partner the thesis was built on, has now fully exited
priceNote: Live price Aug 13 07:49, -1.43% today. Prior report (Aug 4) used $5.65 — -14.5% drift. That report was written TWO DAYS BEFORE the Aug 6 Q2 print and its entire analyst-target basis (Northland $26, Wedbush $22, Oppenheimer $20, consensus $18.45) predates the cuts that followed.
summary: ⚠️ THESIS BROKEN — this replaces the Aug 4 report, whose catalyst was the Aug 6 Q2 print and which assumed a consensus of $18.45. That print landed badly and the assumption is void. Q2 revenue came in at $3.2M against a $3.92M consensus with a wider-than-expected loss, Uber delivery growth REVERSED, and management cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $9-10M. Uber has since divested its entire stake — the partner the whole delivery thesis rested on. Analysts followed: Oppenheimer cut $20 → $7, Guggenheim $13 → $7, Ladenburg $16 → $15, and Cantor Fitzgerald downgraded to Neutral and withdrew its target outright. The stale $18.45 consensus still sitting on the board is what made this pick screen as the best risk/reward available — it is not. Treat any residual bullish framing from the prior version as void.

catalysts.name: Post-Uber Partnership Replacement
catalysts.description: With Uber fully divested, the open question is whether Serve can sign a replacement demand partner at comparable volume. No announced date — this is the thesis-critical unknown, not a scheduled event.

catalysts.name: Diligent Robotics Healthcare Diversification
catalysts.description: Healthcare robotics as a second leg away from food delivery. Genuinely undated and early — optionality, not a near-term catalyst, and it cannot offset a halved delivery guide in 2026.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: First print against the reduced $9-10M guide. The test is whether the cut was conservative enough to beat, or the start of a trend.

risks: Uber fully divested its stake — the anchor partner and demand channel behind the original thesis is gone, not merely reduced
2026 revenue guidance cut to $9-10M, and Q2 delivery volume went backwards rather than merely growing slower
Two analysts cut to $7 (Oppenheimer from $20, Guggenheim from $13) and Cantor withdrew its target entirely — the target range is now bimodal and near the current price, not above it
At a $373M cap on $9-10M of guided revenue, the multiple still prices a growth story that just stopped growing
Cash burn against a halved revenue plan makes a dilutive raise materially more likely

The prior report screened this as the best R/R on the board (17:1) purely because its stale $18.45 consensus survived a print that invalidated it — a warning about the board's inputs, not a feature of this stock
